question: What was the callsign of the trainee in flight?
options: Correct callsign used
Wrong callsign used
procedureDetails: Callsign for flight will be Qatari {callsign_num}CR.

question: Was the Main Switch turned on correctly?
options: Yes, correctly switched on
No, trainee first tried to turn on engines instead of main switch
procedureDetails: The Main Switch must be turned on first before starting the engines.

question: When were both engines started?
options: Both started one by one
Both started together
procedureDetails: First Start Engine 1, wait for N1 to become 20% (will show as a green box), then start the 2nd Engine and wait for it to also reach 20% N1 (green box).

question: When were the Beacon and NAV Lights turned on?
options: Lights turned on when the 1st engine was started
Lights turned on after both engines were started
procedureDetails: Beacon and NAV lights must be turned on immediately prior to starting the first engine to indicate the aircraft is about to move or start engines.

question: When did the trainee announce Taxi?
options: Before starting taxi. ✅
There was significant gap between announcement and movement. ⚠️
Duplicated announcements ⚠️
There was no announcement 💀
Announcement done to wrong runway 💀
procedureDetails: Taxi announcement should be made before commencing taxi and for the correct desired runway

question: What was the ground speed during straight line taxiing?
options: Ground speed was less than or equal to 25 knots
Ground speed exceeded 25 knots
procedureDetails: During straight line taxiing, maintain a ground speed of 25 knots or less to ensure safe aircraft control.

question: What was the ground speed during 90-degree turns?
options: Ground speed was less than 10 knots
Ground speed was 10 knots or more
procedureDetails: When performing a 90-degree turn, ground speed should be reduced to less than 10 knots to prevent excessive side loads on the landing gear and maintain safety.

question: How well was the taxiway centerline maintained during taxi?
options: Nicely Done ✅
Average 🙂
Bad ⚠️
procedureDetails: Keep the aircraft aligned with the taxiway centerline at all times.

question: Was stopping at the Hold Short Line required and completed correctly?
options: Yes, Hold Short was required and completed correctly ✅
Yes, Hold Short was required but not completed correctly ⚠️
No, Hold Short was not required during this flight ✅
procedureDetails: When stopping at HSL, ensure entire aircraft starting from nose should be behind the line and not just the front landing gear

question: If the Trainee made a Hold-Short did they announce holding?
options: Yes, they did ✅
They did but a bit late or a bit early ⚠️
No, they didn't 💀
Hold short was not required ( optional )
procedureDetails: Hold short should only be announced when another plane is taking off or landing on the runway

question: When were the landing and strobes turned on during takeoff?
options: Landing and strobe lights were turned on while entering the runway ✅
Landing and strobe lights were turned on at taxiway ⚠️
Landing and strobe lights were turned on after entering the runway ⚠️
Landing and strobe lights (or either one) were not turned on ❌
procedureDetails: Landing and strobe lights to be turned on while entering the runway

question: Was the take off call made at the correct time?
options: Take off call was made before entering the runway ✅
Take off call was made after entering the runway ⚠️
Take off call was made too early ⚠️
Take off call was not made ⚠️
procedureDetails: The departure announcement should be made before entering the runway for takeoff. This ensures other traffic is aware of your intentions before departure.

question: Was the correct takeoff call direction announced?
options: Departure direction was announced correctly ✅
Pattern call was announced instead of a departure direction ⚠️
Incorrect departure direction was announced ⚠️
No departure direction was announced ⚠️
procedureDetails: The takeoff announcement should include the correct runway and intended direction of departure, typically referencing the direction of the arrival airport or destination.

question: What was the takeoff power during departure?
options: Throttle during takeoff was 100% or N1 exceeding 95 ⚠️
N1 during departure was under realistic limits ✅
procedureDetails: For A320 family N1 should be under 95 (ideally between 89-91 )

question: What speed was the aircraft rotated at?
options: Aircraft rotation occurred at speed beyond 160 knots ⚠️
Aircraft rotation was under the 160 knots limit ✅
procedureDetails: Ideal rotation speed for A320 family is under 160 knots or depending upon weight

question: Were the correct flap settings used during takeoff and initial climb?
options: Flaps 1 used ✅
No flaps used ⚠️
More than 1 flaps used ⚠️
procedureDetails: For the A320 family, flaps 1 is normally used for departure

question: Was the landing gear retracted at the appropriate time after takeoff?
options: Landing gear was retracted at an appropriate altitude and stage of departure ✅
Minor deviations in landing gear retraction timing observed ⚠️
Landing gear was retracted significantly too early, too late, or not managed appropriately during departure ⚠️
procedureDetails: Landing gear is typically retracted as soon as the aircraft achieves a positive rate of climb (100ft-400ft). Following a positive rate of climb after takeoff, the landing gear should be retracted in accordance with standard operating procedures

question: Was the centerline maintained during takeoff?
options: Trainee failed to maintain centerline during takeoff ⚠️
Trainee maintained centerline correctly ✅
Trainee almost exited the runway during takeoff 💀
procedureDetails: Centerline should always be maintained and MUST be aided with the use of rudder in case of crosswind takeoffs

question: Was the aircraft maintained at an appropriate climb rate during takeoff?
options: Climb rate was maintained within the correct range throughout initial climb, ensuring a smooth and stable departure profile ✅
Minor deviations in vertical speed during initial climb observed ⚠️
Significant deviations or unstable climb rate during takeoff observed ⚠️
procedureDetails: Maintain a climb rate of approximately 1000–1500 ft/min during initial climb. Adjust smoothly to maintain positive climb and safe airspeed while ensuring a stable departure profile.

question: Were landing lights turned OFF above 10k feet?
options: Yes, Landing lights were turned off above 10k feet ✅
No, Landing lights were not turned off above 10k feet ⚠️
Lights were turned off too late/early ⚠️
procedureDetails: Landing Lights should always be turned OFF above 10k feet and ON below 10k feet.

question: Was the aircraft operated with an appropriate vertical speed during climb phases?
options: Vertical speed maintained within appropriate limits throughout the flight ✅
Minor deviations in vertical speed observed during climb ⚠️
Excessive or unstable vertical speeds observed during climb ⚠️
procedureDetails: For the A320 family, the vertical speeds should be 2500 until 5k feet, 2000 until FL140, 1500 until FL240 and 1000 until cruise

question: Was the cruise altitude selected in accordance with the assigned flight direction?
options: Correct cruise altitude selected for the flight direction ✅
Cruise altitude selected was acceptable but not optimal for the flight direction ⚠️
Incorrect cruise altitude selected for the flight direction ⚠️
procedureDetails:
If plane is flying Eastbound flight then its Cruise Altitude should be in ODD numbers (FL230,FL250,FL270,FL290,FL310,FL330,FL350.)
- If plane is flying Westbound flight then its Cruise Altitude should be in EVEN numbers (FL240,FL260,FL280,FL300,FL320,FL340,FL360.)

question: Was the aircraft operated at the appropriate cruise speed throughout the cruise phase?
options: Speed maintained accurately throughout the cruise phase ✅
Minor speed deviations observed during cruise ⚠️ (M0.77 or M0.79)
Significant speed deviations observed during cruise ⚠️
procedureDetails: For the A320 family, the typical cruise speed is Mach 0.78

question: Were landing lights turned ON below 10k feet?
options: Landing lights were turned ON below 10k feet ✅
Landing lights were not turned ON below 10k feet ⚠️
Lights were not turned ON ❌
procedureDetails: Landing Lights should always be turned ON below 10k feet

question: Were appropriate inbound and traffic advisories communicated during the flight on UNICOM?
options: All required inbound and traffic announcements were made correctly ✅
Minor mistakes or timing issues observed in inbound/traffic announcements ⚠️
Required inbound and traffic announcements were frequently missed, incorrect, or not made ⚠️
procedureDetails: The announcement had to be like this: Inbound for landing -> will make Left/Right traffic for runway _ -> Left/Right downwind runway _ -> Left/Right base runway _ -> Final runway _

question: Was the aircraft configured with the appropriate flap settings during the arrival and approach phases?
options: Flaps were deployed at the correct speeds throughout the approach ✅
Deviation from standard flap usage or improper configuration observed ⚠️
procedureDetails: For the A320 family, flap deployment should generally follow these procedures

question: Was the landing gear deployed at the appropriate point during the approach phase?
options: Landing gear was deployed at the correct distance/altitude, ensuring a stabilized final approach profile ✅
Minor deviations in landing gear deployment timing observed ⚠️
Significant deviations such as early or late gear deployment observed ⚠️
procedureDetails: Deploy landing gear around 4–5 NM from the airport or below 2000 ft AGL. Ensure gear is down early enough to stabilize the approach before final descent.

question: Was the autopilot disengaged at the appropriate point during the approach?
options: Autopilot was disengaged at the correct altitude or distance from the runway ✅
Autopilot was disengaged slightly earlier or later than recommended ⚠️
Autopilot was disengaged significantly outside the recommended parameters ⚠️
Did not disengage Auto Pilot 💀
procedureDetails: Autopilot should be disengaged at approximately 1000 ft AGL or 2 NM from the runway, whichever occurs first. This allows sufficient time for a stable manual approach and landing. AP landing may be allowed but its dependent on winds

question: How effectively was the runway centerline maintained during landing and rollout?
options: Runway centerline maintained accurately throughout landing and rollout ✅
Minor deviations or Significant deviations from the runway centerline were observed ⚠️
procedureDetails: Aircraft should always maintain centerline during Landing and if Crosswind is high then Rudder must be used to counter it .

question: How effectively were the spoilers deployed after landing?
options: Spoilers were deployed promptly after touchdown and operated correctly ✅
Spoilers were deployed with a slight delay after touchdown ⚠️
Spoilers were not deployed or were deployed incorrectly ⚠️
procedureDetails: Spoilers should be deployed immediately after touchdown to reduce lift, improve wheel braking effectiveness, and assist in decelerating the aircraft during rollout.

question: How effectively was reverse thrust applied during landing rollout?
options: Reverse thrust was applied promptly and appropriately after touchdown (<60%) ✅
Reverse thrust was not applied correctly or was omitted (>60%) ⚠️
Reverse thrust was not applied ⚠️
procedureDetails: Plane RT must be disengaged by 60 knots and its should not used more than 50-60%

question: Was Clear Of All Runways announced properly?
options: Clear of all runways was announced at the correct time immediately after exiting the runway and crossing the hold short line ✅
Delay in issuing the “clear of all runways” call observed ⚠️
Clear of all runways never announced ⚠️
procedureDetails: The “clear of all runways” call should only be made once the aircraft has fully exited the runway and crossed the hold short line.

category: Landing and Strobe Lights Post-Landing Procedure
question: How efficient was the Landing and Strobe lights usage after landing?
options: Lights were turned off at/directly after the hold-short line. ✅
Lights were turned off after passing the Hold-Short line ⚠️
Lights were turned off while still on the runway/at the gate. 💀
Lights wasn't turned off/ was never on 💀
procedureDetails: Lights must be turned back off as soon as the plane leaves the runway. While being on the hold-short line or directly after crossing it.

question: How well was the taxiway centerline maintained during taxi on arrival airport?
options: Nicely Done ✅
Average 🙂
Bad ⚠️
procedureDetails: Keep the aircraft aligned with the taxiway centerline at all times.
